When Cursor is selected **and** the repo already has `.cursor/environment.json`, enable appends `bash .entire/install-cli.sh` to that file’s `install` command. It does **not** create `.cursor/environment.json`. A committed copy overrides dashboard-managed personal/team Cloud Agent environments. If the file is missing, enable prints the one-liner to add in the dashboard. If `install` already puts Entire on PATH (this repo’s `.cursor/install.sh` is the example), it is left unchanged. Agents that boot in a remote environment can implement `CloudCLIInstaller` the same way Cursor does. ## Cursor Cloud transcripts Managed Cursor Cloud VMs can send `transcript_path: null` and never create the local `~/.cursor/projects/.../agent-transcripts` directory; conversation history remains remote-only. Previously Entire fabricated that local path, waited five seconds on every `stop`, then aborted turn-end before git-based file detection, stop-hook token capture, phase transition, or checkpoint creation. Cursor transcript resolution now uses this precedence: 1. Hook JSON `transcript_path` 2. Cursor’s documented `CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH` hook environment variable 3. Existing local Cursor CLI/IDE layout fallback If the fallback’s parent directory is absent, Cursor skips the impossible flush wait and turn-end continues without transcript bytes. [#2112](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2112) separately fixes Cursor presence detection and is intentionally not duplicated here. ## Review follow-up Deselecting Cursor through the manage-agents path (`applyAgentChanges`) now calls `RemoveCloudCLIInstall`, matching `entire disable` and a later `entire enable` that drops the agent. Rewrites of an existing `.cursor/environment.json` keep the file’s previous permission bits. This only extends what enable already writes for a selected agent; it does not promote a command into agent-help listing or read-only. ## Testing - `mise run check` (fmt, lint, unit, integration, e2e canary) - `TestApplyAgentChanges_RemovesCursorCloudInstall` covers manage-agents teardown - Ensure/remove tests assert Unix `0600` is preserved when rewriting `environment.json` `mise run dup:staged` reports only a pre-existing duplicate pair in `lifecycle_test.go` (`SessionStart_EmptySessionID` / `TurnStart_EmptySessionID`); no new duplication was reported.

description: Which Cursor surfaces Entire can actually capture, verified 2026-08-24 against Cursor IDE 3.0.12 / CLI 2026.08.11 — plus the #1262 half-fix that made the gap silent
metadata:

---

Measured, not inferred. `cmd/entire/cli/agent/cursor/AGENT.md` was probed
2026-03-02 and is stale in at least two ways: it lists 9 hooks (Cursor now
documents ~21) and claims the CLI uses the flat transcript layout
`<dir>/<id>.jsonl` — build 2026.08.11 used the **nested** IDE layout, which
`ResolveSessionFile` already prefers, so nothing broke.

| surface | hooks that fire | capture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI interactive (tmux) | SessionStart, TurnStart, TurnEnd, SessionEnd | **works** — verified end to end |
| CLI headless `-p` | sessionStart + sessionEnd ONLY | **nothing** — no TurnStart, so no session state is created |
| cloud / mobile agents | beforeSubmitPrompt, stop, tool hooks; NOT sessionStart/sessionEnd | needs `entire` installed in the cloud env |

Headless is the inverse of cloud: each fires one half of the pair. Headless is
**fixable, not a platform limit** — the transcript IS written to disk and
`sessionEnd` carries `conversation_id`, which `resolveTranscriptRef` can already
resolve. State creation is just bolted to TurnStart.

**`sessionStart` supports `additional_context` and it reaches the model.**
Verified with a random sentinel echoed back verbatim on CLI 2026.08.11. So a
Cursor `ContextInjector` is viable. Cursor honors `additional_context`, NOT
Claude's `additionalContext`, so `RenderAdditionalContextHookOutput` won't work
as-is. There are open forum reports saying it never injects; they did not
reproduce here (likely IDE- or Windows-specific, or fixed).

**Cursor still has no user-facing banner channel.** `user_message` exists only
on gating/deny paths (preToolUse, beforeShellExecution, beforeSubmitPrompt-when-
blocked) plus preCompact. There is no unconditional "show the user this at
session start", so the "Entire CLI will link this conversation" banner genuinely
cannot be delivered — that half of the gap is the platform, not us.

**Why the detection gap mattered so much (the #1262 story).** #1262 fixed the
case where a Cursor session in a Claude-Code-only repo was *claimed* by Claude's
forwarded hooks and misattributed; `fadc4a06a` added `hook_guard.go`, which
declines the forwarded hook. Correct — but it converted a *visible* wrong-agent
bug into *silent* zero capture for anyone whose repo never got Cursor hooks. And
they never got them because `DetectPresence` only checked `<repo>/.cursor/`,
while Cursor keeps per-project state in `~/.cursor/projects/<sanitized-path>/`.
Worse than being skipped: `enable` fell back to the DEFAULT agent and wired
Claude Code, printing "Ready." Fixed in PR #2112. See [[cursor-detection-e2e-blindspots]].

**Sidecar store already mapped.** `images.go:51,140-165` locates
`~/.cursor/chats/<workspace-hash>/<session-id>/store.db` for image blobs only.
`meta.json` next to it carries `cwd`, so workspace-hash → repo is resolvable if
a transcript ever needs to come from there.

name: cursor-detection-e2e-blindspots
description: Why the whole test suite could not catch the Cursor detection bug — E2E always pins --agent, so no test ever exercises agent auto-detection
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The Cursor detection bug (PR #2112) shipped despite E2E running a full
`cursor-cli` leg. Three independent reasons, each sufficient:

1. **E2E cannot reach the detection code.** Every E2E test enables Entire via
   one helper: `e2e/entire/entire.go:24-27` → `enable --agent <name>`. That flag
   "Enables non-interactive mode" and bypasses `selectAgents`/`DetectPresence`
   entirely. The suite always *tells* Entire which agent it is testing.
2. **The one bare-`enable` test asserts the wrong things.**
   `integration_test/setup_cmd_test.go:174-205` checks stdout contains
   `"Ready."` and `settings["enabled"] == true`. Both were true while Cursor was
   silently unwired and Claude Code was wired instead. It never asserts *which*
   agent got hooks. `selectAgents` has zero unit tests.
3. **`TestDetectPresence_NoCursorDir` encoded the narrow behavior as correct.**
   Asserting false for a bare temp dir is right in isolation, but that is also
   the exact state of a real Cursor user's repo, so the test read as
   confirmation rather than a gap.

**Why:** coverage was written against the harness's assumptions, not the user's
starting conditions. E2E begins from "Entire is enabled for agent X" and
verifies what happens next; nothing verifies how a repo *gets* there — which is
where a first-timer actually lives.

**How to apply:** when a bug is reported about onboarding or setup, do not look
for it in E2E — E2E starts downstream of setup. Reproduce by hand with a real
binary and no flags. And when adding an agent, add a detection test that starts
from the agent's own state directory, not from a repo-local config dir; agents
whose config lives in `$HOME` (Cursor) are invisible to the repo-local check.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cloud Agent install script for the Entire CLI.
#
# Idempotent: safe to run repeatedly and against a cached/partially-prepared
# snapshot. It prepares the mise-pinned toolchain, downloads Go modules, and
# builds the CLI. It does NOT start any long-running process.
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "${REPO_ROOT}"

log() { printf '\n\033[1m[install]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

# 1. Ensure git supports the reftable ref-format. The test suite creates a
#    reftable repository with `git init --ref-format=reftable`, and Ubuntu 24.04
#    ships git 2.43 (ref-format was stabilised in 2.45). Probe the actual
#    feature rather than parsing the version string (packaged/backported builds
#    have unreliable version strings), and upgrade from the git-core PPA when it
#    is missing (or when git itself is absent).
git_supports_reftable() {
  command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  local probe ok=1
  probe="$(mktemp -d)"
  git init -q --ref-format=reftable "${probe}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok=0
  rm -rf "${probe}"
  return "${ok}"
}

if ! git_supports_reftable; then
  log "Installing/upgrading git for reftable support (have $(git --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}' || echo none))"
  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update -qq
  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends software-properties-common
  sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:git-core/ppa
  sudo apt-get update -qq
  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y git
fi
log "git $(git --version | awk '{print $3}') (reftable supported)"

# 2. Ensure mise (task runner + toolchain manager) is installed and on PATH.
if ! command -v mise >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [ ! -x "${HOME}/.local/bin/mise" ]; then
    log "Installing mise"
    curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh
  fi
  export PATH="${HOME}/.local/bin:${PATH}"
fi
log "mise $(mise --version)"

# 3. Make mise + its shims available in interactive agent terminals.
BASHRC="${HOME}/.bashrc"
if [ -w "${BASHRC}" ] || [ ! -e "${BASHRC}" ]; then
  if ! grep -q 'mise activate bash' "${BASHRC}" 2>/dev/null; then
    cat >> "${BASHRC}" <<'MISE_ACTIVATE'
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
command -v mise >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "$(mise activate bash)"
MISE_ACTIVATE
  fi
fi

# 4. Install the pinned toolchain (Go, golangci-lint, gotestsum, shellcheck,
#    tmux, and the roger-roger E2E helper binaries) declared in mise.toml.
mise trust --yes
mise install
eval "$(mise activate bash --shims)"

# 5. Download Go modules and build the CLI to prove the toolchain works.
log "Downloading Go modules"
go mod download

log "Building the entire CLI"
go build -o entire ./cmd/entire/
./entire version

# 6. Put `entire` on PATH. This repo dogfoods Entire: it commits agent hook
#    configs (.cursor/hooks.json, .claude/settings.json, ...) that invoke the
#    bare `entire` command and no-op when it is not found. Making the built
#    binary discoverable is all the environment needs — Entire installs its own
#    git hooks on the first turn-start hook (strategy.EnsureSetup reinstalls them
#    when absent). Prefer /usr/local/bin (on the standard PATH hooks run with);
#    fall back to ~/.local/bin when sudo is unavailable.
log "Putting entire on PATH"
if ! sudo -n ln -sf "${REPO_ROOT}/entire" /usr/local/bin/entire 2>/dev/null; then
  mkdir -p "${HOME}/.local/bin"
  ln -sf "${REPO_ROOT}/entire" "${HOME}/.local/bin/entire"
fi
log "entire on PATH: $(command -v entire || echo MISSING)"

content.text:
I reviewed the full diff, the surrounding code paths, and verified the external claims (Cursor's `CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH` is genuinely documented; `scripts/install.sh` really does hardcode `$HOME/.local/bin`). CI is green and the three bot findings are already addressed in the follow-up commits.

## Verdict

The shape is right: capability interface for the wiring, never creating `environment.json`, fail-open scoped to one agent. Two findings would bite real users, and one is a silent side effect the PR body doesn't mention.

---

### 1. The appended install step can break the user's Cloud environment build

`cloudenv/install.go:23` — `InstallCLIStep = "bash .entire/install-cli.sh"`, appended with `&&`.

Two ways this fails hard, and in both the *user's whole environment setup* fails, not just Entire:

**Missing file.** For this to work, both `.cursor/environment.json` *and* `.entire/install-cli.sh` must be committed. `environment.json` is usually already tracked, so a user commits the one-line change and not the new untracked helper. On the Cloud VM `bash .entire/install-cli.sh` exits 127 and the `&&` chain fails. The README says to commit it; the enable output (`cursor.go:74`) does not.

**Wrong cwd.** The step is repo-relative but inherits whatever cwd the preceding steps left. `"cd frontend && npm ci"` becomes `"cd frontend && npm ci && bash .entire/install-cli.sh"` — runs in `frontend/`, file not found, install fails. Monorepo install commands `cd` all the time. Notably this repo's own `.cursor/install.sh` doesn't trust cwd either; it recomputes `REPO_ROOT` from `BASH_SOURCE`.

Fix either by making the step self-locating and non-fatal (`r="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"; [ -f "$r/.entire/install-cli.sh" ] && bash "$r/.entire/install-cli.sh"`), or keep it strict and have `EnsureCursorEnvironment` print "commit `.entire/install-cli.sh` and `.cursor/environment.json`" alongside the ✓. I'd do both.

### 2. `AppendInstallStep` eats a trailing `&` (background operator)

`cloudenv/install.go:126` — `strings.TrimRight(install, " \t;&")`.

Intended for a trailing `&&`, but it strips a single `&` too: `"./devserver.sh &"` → `"./devserver.sh && bash .entire/install-cli.sh"`, turning a backgrounded command into a blocking one. `StripInstallStep` can't undo it either, so `entire disable` leaves the mutated command behind. Trim whitespace and `;`, then strip a trailing `&&` explicitly.

### 3. Detection and removal use different matching, so stale wiring survives disable

`MentionsEntireInstall` matches the substring `.entire/install-cli.sh` (`install.go:60`), but `StripInstallStep` (`install.go:130`) only removes an exact ` && <step>` suffix or a sole exact match. A step that was hand-moved, reordered, or written by a future CLI whose `InstallCLIStep` text differs is seen as "already wired" (so enable skips it) but never removed by disable. Cheap fix: strip on the same `.entire/install-cli.sh` marker.

### 4. Fail-open truncates a previously-good stored transcript

`lifecycle.go:781-794` — when `transcriptAvailable` is false, `transcriptData` stays nil and `os.WriteFile(logFile, storedTranscript, 0o600)` still runs, overwriting `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` with zero bytes.

For Cursor Cloud there was never content, so no loss. But mid-session it's reachable: `resolveTranscriptRef` now has three sources, and a turn that resolves to a path whose parent is absent (env var set on some hooks but not others, `~/.cursor` cleared, project dir rotated) truncates a session log that earlier turns populated. The consequence is out of proportion to the trigger — per the `CheckpointTranscriptSize` / `sessionHasNewContent` coupling in CLAUDE.md, a shrinking transcript makes the growth comparison false and the session silently stops condensing. Guard the write: skip it when `!transcriptAvailable` and a non-empty `full.jsonl` already exists.

### 5. Undocumented side effect: subagent events now get a fabricated `SessionRef`

`cursor/lifecycle.go` — `parseSubagentStart` / `parseSubagentStop` switched from `raw.TranscriptPath` to `resolveTranscriptRef(...)`. That feeds `completeSubagentTaskRecord`, and it cuts both ways:

- Good: `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(filepath.Dir(event.SessionRef), ...)` (`lifecycle.go:1495`) previously probed under `filepath.Dir("")` = `.`. Now it probes the real session dir, so the subagent transcript is actually findable.
- Risky: in the foreground path, `transcriptToScan = event.SessionRef` (`lifecycle.go:1532`) falls back to the **parent** transcript scanned from offset 0. Cursor used to hit `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset`'s empty-path early return (`cursor/transcript.go:158`) and contribute nothing; now the whole session's `FileModificationTools` hits can be attributed to one subagent task — exactly the hazard the comment 30 lines above calls out for the background path. Note AGENT.md's "transcript lacks tool_use blocks" is stale (Cursor's own extractor reads them), so this isn't inert by construction.

Either confirm it's harmless with a test, or fabricate only for the events that need it.

### 6. `TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_MissingTranscriptParent_Continues` asserts almost nothing

```go
if err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), "transcript file not found") {
```
Any *other* error passes. The point of the fail-open is that turn-end reaches git file detection, token capture, and the phase transition — assert `err == nil` and that a step/checkpoint was actually saved, otherwise the test survives a regression that breaks the whole tail.

---

### Smaller things

- **`.entire/install-cli.sh` is written for every agent** (`setup.go:2142`, inside `setupEntireDirectory`), so a Claude-Code-only repo gets a Cursor-Cloud bootstrap it never runs, `entire disable` never removes it, and a hand-edited copy is silently overwritten on the next `enable`. Per CLAUDE.md's "flag it, don't decide it", worth stating in the PR why it's unconditional rather than gated on `CloudCLIInstaller`.
- **Non-atomic rewrite of a file Entire doesn't own** — `writeCursorEnv` (`cloudenv/cursor.go:115`) uses `os.WriteFile`, while `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic` is right there in the package already imported. The agent hook writers use plain `os.WriteFile` too, so this matches local precedent — but those are files Entire owns, and a truncated `environment.json` breaks the user's Cloud env.
- **`commandMentionsEntire` markers are checks, not installs** — `"command -v entire"` matches a script that merely *tests* for the binary (and `/usr/local/bin/entire` matches an `rm`). False positive means enable silently declines to wire.
- **`maxScriptScanBytes` truncates after the read** (`install.go:75`) — `os.ReadFile` has already pulled the whole file into memory by then.
- **`TestDispatchLifecycleEvent_UnknownEventType` gained `ag.name = agent.AgentNameCursor`** (`lifecycle_test.go:382`) with no explanation. The dispatcher returns on the `default:` branch before the name is consulted, so this looks like leftover noise — it narrows a deliberately generic test.
- **`doctor` doesn't know about this.** It's the natural place to catch "environment.json lost the step" or "install-cli.sh isn't committed", which is the exact silent-no-op class this PR exists to fix. Follow-up, not a blocker.
- **`cloudenv/cursor.go` in a generic package** — the Cursor-specific `.cursor/environment.json` logic sits in `cloudenv` while the thin capability wrapper sits in `agent/cursor`. There's no import cycle forcing that split; the Cursor half would read better in the cursor package.

Nothing here is a correctness problem in the happy path — #1 is the one I'd fix before merge, since its failure mode is "the user's Cloud Agent stops booting" rather than "Entire doesn't capture".

func TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_MissingTranscriptParent_Continues(t *testing.T) {
	// Cannot use t.Parallel() because we use t.Chdir().
	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "init.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "init.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")
	t.Chdir(tmpDir)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()

	// Modify a file so the whole turn-end tail (SaveStep included) has to run:
	// the point of failing open is that git-based capture, stop-hook tokens,
	// and the phase transition still happen, not merely that no error escapes.
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(tmpDir, "init.txt"), []byte("changed"), 0o600))

	// Cloud Agent layout: computed session_ref points under a directory that
	// was never created.
	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(tmpDir, "agent-transcripts", "cloud-sess.jsonl")

	const sessionID = "cloud-sess"
	ag := newMockAgent()
	ag.name = agent.AgentNameCursor
	event := &agent.Event{
		Type:       agent.TurnEnd,
		SessionID:  sessionID,
		SessionRef: transcriptPath,
		Timestamp:  time.Now(),
		TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 11, OutputTokens: 7, APICallCount: 1},
	}

	require.NoError(t, handleLifecycleTurnEnd(context.Background(), ag, event),
		"turn-end must fail open when the local transcript layout is absent")

	state, err := strategy.LoadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state, "the checkpoint must still be saved without a transcript")
	require.Contains(t, state.FilesTouched, "init.txt",
		"git-based file detection must still run when the transcript is unavailable")
	require.NotNil(t, state.TokenUsage, "stop-hook token fields must still be captured")
	require.Equal(t, 11, state.TokenUsage.InputTokens)
}

// TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_MissingTranscriptParent_KeepsEarlierTranscript
// covers the fail-open path landing mid-session. Writing the (empty) transcript
// unconditionally would drop the session log captured earlier and, worse, make
// the stored copy shrink — which freezes sessionHasNewContent's growth
// comparison and silently stops the session condensing.
func TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_MissingTranscriptParent_KeepsEarlierTranscript(t *testing.T) {
	// Cannot use t.Parallel() because we use t.Chdir().
	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "init.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "init.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")
	t.Chdir(tmpDir)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(tmpDir, "init.txt"), []byte("changed"), 0o600))

	const sessionID = "cloud-sess-late"
	sessionDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
	sessionDirAbs, err := paths.AbsPath(context.Background(), sessionDir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(sessionDirAbs, 0o750))
	captured := []byte(`{"type":"user","message":"captured by an earlier turn"}` + "\n")
	logFile := filepath.Join(sessionDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName)
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(logFile, captured, 0o600))

	ag := newMockAgent()
	ag.name = agent.AgentNameCursor
	event := &agent.Event{
		Type:       agent.TurnEnd,
		SessionID:  sessionID,
		SessionRef: filepath.Join(tmpDir, "agent-transcripts", sessionID+".jsonl"),
		Timestamp:  time.Now(),
	}

	require.NoError(t, handleLifecycleTurnEnd(context.Background(), ag, event))

	after, err := os.ReadFile(logFile) //nolint:gosec // test-controlled path
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, string(captured), string(after),
		"a transcript-less turn must not truncate the copy an earlier turn stored")
}

content.text:
Fixed and verified on branch `cursor/cursor-cloud-env-entire-cli-2123`, uncommitted.

## What changed

**1. The install step can no longer break the Cloud environment build.** `cloudenv.InstallCLIStep` is now:
```
bash "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.entire/install-cli.sh" || true
```
Repo-root-relative (survives an earlier `cd` in the `&&` chain) and non-fatal (a helper that wasn't committed yet prints a diagnostic instead of failing the whole install). Verified in a real shell from a subdirectory, both with and without the helper present — chain exit 0 in both cases. `entire enable` now also prints the commit hint naming both files.

**2. `AppendInstallStep` no longer eats a trailing `&`.** It strips only `&&`/`;`, and when the command genuinely ends in a background `&` it joins with a space (`cmd & step`) rather than producing the syntax error `cmd & && step`.

**3. Detect and remove now agree.** `StripInstallStep` keys on the new `InstallCLIMarker` (`.entire/install-cli.sh`) instead of the exact step text, removes the step wherever it sits in the chain along with its joining operator, and preserves surrounding bytes. So a step written by an older CLI — or moved by hand — is actually removed by `entire disable`. Added an append→strip round-trip test over several install shapes.

**4. A transcript-less turn can't truncate an earlier one.** `handleLifecycleTurnEnd` now skips the write when the transcript is unavailable and a non-empty `full.jsonl` already exists (new `fileHasContent` in `utils.go`). Confirmed the new test fails without the guard — the previous behavior zeroed the stored transcript, which is what freezes `sessionHasNewContent` and silently stops the session condensing.

Largely agree. I went through what the helper does that a bare one-liner wouldn't, and it comes to one line.

```bash
command -v entire && exit 0        # saves a download; installer re-runs fine anyway
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
[[ -x ~/.local/bin/entire ]] || fail
export PATH=...                    # dies with the script
persist_path ~/.bashrc ~/.profile  # only helps interactive/login shells
sudo -n ln -sf "$BIN" /usr/local/bin/entire || true   # ← the only load-bearing line
command -v entire || fail
```

Hooks are non-interactive subprocesses of the agent, so `.bashrc`/`.profile` never get sourced for them. That leaves the `/usr/local/bin` symlink as the sole reason the wrapper exists — and this repo's own `.cursor/install.sh` already says so out loud: *"Prefer /usr/local/bin (on the standard PATH hooks run with); fall back to ~/.local/bin when sudo is unavailable."*

And that job belongs in `scripts/install.sh`, not in a file committed into every user's repo. I checked: the installer hardcodes `DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"` with no env or flag override (`--channel` is the only flag), and it never persists PATH — it just *prints* the `export PATH=…` line for the user to paste. The helper is a wrapper compensating for the installer stopping one step short.

Fix it upstream and the Cloud step becomes a literal one-liner with no second file:

```
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```

That deletes an entire class of problem rather than hardening it — which is most of what I spent the last hour on:

- No "both files must be committed" failure mode → the commit hint, the `|| true`, and the `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` wrapper all become unnecessary (a curl pipe is cwd-independent for free).
- No `.entire/install-cli.sh` landing in every repo regardless of agent, no `entire disable` leaving it behind, no churn when the embedded copy changes.
- `entire.io/install.sh` becomes the strip/detect marker — it's already one of them.
- `Append`/`Strip`/`MentionsEntireInstall` still earn their keep (you're still editing someone's install command), and findings #4–#6 are untouched — they're transcript-side.

Worth noting the redirect resolves to `raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/cli/refs/heads/main/scripts/install.sh`, so an installer change ships the moment it merges — no release needed, but it also lands on everyone's `curl | bash` immediately.

**The one thing I can't answer from here:** whether `~/.local/bin` is already on PATH for a Cursor Cloud hook subprocess. If it is, the one-liner is complete as written. If it isn't, the installer needs to reach a dir that is — and since `/usr/local/bin` needs sudo, the cleanest version is teaching `install.sh` to try `sudo -n ln -sf` into `/usr/local/bin` after a successful install and fall back silently, i.e. moving that one line up a level. Either way the committed helper goes.

The steelman for keeping it — reviewable, pinnable, reusable across hosts — doesn't survive contact: the script's body *is* `curl | bash`, so it isn't meaningfully more auditable, and the reuse unit other hosts need is the URL, not a repo-local file.

Want me to rework it that way? Concretely: drop the helper and its embed, add the PATH/dir handling to `scripts/install.sh`, retarget the marker at `entire.io/install.sh`, and drop the fixes that only existed to protect the two-file arrangement. That shrinks the PR rather than growing it.

```json
"install": "cd frontend && npm ci && curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash"
```

## What went away

- `cloudenv/install.sh` and `cloudenv/embed.go` — deleted.
- `WriteInstallScript` and its two call sites, including the unconditional write in `setupEntireDirectory`. No repo now gets a bootstrap file it will never run (verified above: `.entire/` holds only `.gitignore` and `settings.json`).

- **Marker-based detect/strip**, retargeted from the helper path to `entire.io/install.sh`. The legacy test cases were meaningless — the old step never shipped — so I replaced them with a hand-written variant (`curl -sSL … | sh`, different flags and shell, same installer). refactor(cloudenv): install the CLI with the published installer

The committed .entire/install-cli.sh bootstrap only did one thing a bare
`curl | bash` does not: symlink into /usr/local/bin. Everything else it
added was redundant (the installer is safe to re-run) or dead for hooks
(.bashrc/.profile are never sourced for a non-interactive subprocess).

That one job belongs in scripts/install.sh, not in a file committed into
every user's repo, so drop the helper and append the installer directly:

previous step needed a second file committed alongside environment.json

whole install command rather than merely skip itself.

Conflicts resolved, merged, and verified. Everything is committed on the branch.

## The conflict

One file, `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`, two hunks — both from main refactoring the exact code this PR was editing.

**Hunk 1.** Main extracted the duplicated add/reinstall loops in `applyAgentChanges` into a shared `setupAgentHookSet` helper. This PR had changed those same two loops to call `setupAgentHooksAndCloud`. Took main's helper.

**Hunk 2.** The helper's definition landed next to this PR's three new cloud functions. Kept both, and folded the cloud step into the helper:

```go
if _, err := setupAgentHooks(ctx, ag, forceHooks); err != nil { ... continue }
if err := setupCloudCLIInstall(ctx, w, ag); err != nil {
    errs = append(errs, err)
    continue
}
warnCodexHooksAfterSetup(ctx, w, ag)
```

Called separately rather than routed through `setupAgentHooksAndCloud`, deliberately: the helper wraps its error as `failed to setup %s hooks`, so routing the cloud install through it would produce "failed to setup Cursor hooks: failed to set up Cursor cloud environment: …" — re-introducing exactly the double-wrap the earlier bot review made this PR fix.

**A third break git resolved silently but wrongly.** Main also rewrote `removeAgentHooks` to report through an uninstall printer instead of an error slice. Git text-merged this PR's `errs = append(errs, err)` into that function cleanly, and it didn't compile (`undefined: errs`). Adapted to main's vocabulary:

```go
if err := removeCloudCLIInstall(ctx, ag); err != nil {
    builtinProblem = true
    p.warnUnder("%v", err)
}
```

All six cloud wiring points survived (`setup.go:631, 1257, 1674, 1744, 1989, 2869`).

## Worth knowing

Main landed `a61718113 fix(cursor): extract modified files from tool_use blocks` — `ReadSession` now populates `ModifiedFiles` from Cursor's transcript, and the old "Cursor's transcript has no tool_use blocks" comment is gone. That makes the subagent `SessionRef` fix in this PR more load-bearing than when I wrote it: scanning a fabricated *parent* transcript from offset 0 now definitely yields the whole session's files attributed to one task.

Also: `mise run lint` failed once mid-merge with "go module files modified, please commit result of `go mod tidy`". That was the in-progress merge staging making `go.mod`/`go.sum` look dirty — I ran `go mod tidy` and confirmed it's a true no-op. Clean after committing the merge.
